decisions.quote:
In two 

well-powered samples (N = 1920), we conducted a close replication of the default effect in Johnson 

and  Goldstein  (2003)  and  in  Johnson,  Bellman,  and  Lohse  (2002).  We  successfully  replicated 

Johnson and Goldstein (2003).
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent (note: the Luna triage entry for target_index 0 mistakenly discussed Van Dalen and Henkens, 2014, which is target_index 2). Target 0 is Johnson and Goldstein (2003), 'Do defaults save lives?', Science, 302, 1338-1339 (no DOI is printed in the source text or present in the bibliography metadata cache). Chandrashekar et al. (2022) explicitly conduct a direct replication of Experiment 1 of Johnson and Goldstein (2003) (organ donation hypothetical scenario across Opt-In, Opt-Out, and Neutral conditions in two samples totaling N = 1,920; Part 1 of Methods and Results, plus Supplementary Table S7). The only shipped row (row 2383) is Johnson, Bellman, and Lohse (2002) (10.1023/a:1015044207315, Marketing Letters), which is a distinct original study on online health-survey privacy framing replicated in Part 2. Thus Johnson and Goldstein (2003) is a genuine omitted replication target.
